title: A Compass for the Horizon
premise: August Nystrom, a desert ranger who has spent years erasing himself from every record and relationship, is chasing a petty thief when a dying prospector named Odile Vane trades him a map to the Meridian's wreck for one promise: that someone will finish what she started. The map draws August into an unlikely crew—a disgraced cartographer, a stowaway girl with no name of her own, and the thief he was hunting—and forces him to choose between his debt to a dead woman and the family forming around him. As the salvage fleet closes in and the dry season burns toward its end, August learns the wreck holds not treasure but Odile's true legacy: proof of the drowned settlement she came from, and with it, a place where people like him belong. In the end, August surrenders his invisibility—signing his real name to the claim, keeping the promise, and staying with the crew he once planned to abandon.
about_author: Beatrix Ashgrove is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through salt flats and canyon country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who find their way home by getting thoroughly lost.

chapters.title: The Weight of Nothing
chapters.summary: August Nystrom tracks a thief named Cass Merrow across the empty basin, narrating in close third person. He catches her, but she escapes with his rations, leaving him stranded. The chapter establishes his self-imposed isolation and quiet competence. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor—he'd rather lose supplies than make a report that puts his name on paper.

chapters.title: A Dying Woman's Ledger
chapters.summary: Still in August's POV, he finds prospector Odile Vane collapsed at a dry well. She offers him a map to the wreck of the Meridian in exchange for a promise: deliver it where it needs to go. He accepts mostly to end the conversation. She dies at dawn. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation; August realizes promises are debts that outlive the debtor.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: August deciphers the map and learns the salvage fleet, led by Captain Renn Halloway, is already sailing for the coast. He calculates six tides before the channel dries for the season. POV shifts briefly to Halloway, hungry and ruthless. Emotional beat: the clock starts; August understands the map makes him visible whether he likes it or not.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Shame
chapters.summary: August seeks out Edda Lune, a disgraced cartographer who once charted these coasts and can read Odile's markings. She agrees to help—for her own redemption, not his. Cass reappears, caught stealing again, and August, against his judgment, doesn't turn her in. Emotional beat: three strangers bound by failure rather than trust.

chapters.title: What the Girl Carried
chapters.summary: En route to the coast, they discover Cass has been hiding a stowaway: a mute child called Wren, who carries a carved token matching a symbol on Odile's map. Edda recognizes it as the mark of Solmere, the drowned settlement. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open August's cynicism—the map is bigger than treasure, and Wren may be its heir.

chapters.title: Salt and Betrayal
chapters.summary: Halloway's fleet scouts ambush the group at a tidal cave; Edda is injured covering their escape, and Cass confesses she sold word of the map to Halloway weeks ago, before knowing what it meant. August nearly abandons them all. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness colliding—the found family fractures precisely when it matters most.

chapters.title: The Channel Narrows
chapters.summary: Racing the fifth tide, August leads the wounded party through the sinking marsh while Halloway's main ship shadows them. Cass earns back a measure of trust by rigging a decoy fire that delays the fleet. POV alternates between August and a doubting Halloway crewman. Emotional beat: grudging interdependence; August stops counting who owes whom.

chapters.title: The Meridian
chapters.summary: At low tide the wreck emerges from the silt. Inside, they find not gold but Odile's archive: records, charts, and testimony proving Solmere's survivors were wrongfully dispossessed—documents that could restore land and names to hundreds, including Wren's kin. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the true cargo is identity itself, and Halloway arrives as the tide returns.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Climax. Halloway storms the wreck as the channel floods. August, choosing the promise over escape, fights to hold the archive while Cass and Edda ferry documents and Wren out through the rising water. Halloway, offered the fortune he expected and refused the truth he fears, is left stranded by the tide he misjudged. Emotional beat: sacrifice; August finally acts like a man with something to lose.

chapters.title: A Name on the Line
chapters.summary: Resolution. In the rebuilt coastal town of Solmere's descendants, August signs his full name to the registry delivering Odile's claim—his first signature in nine years. Cass stays; Edda begins remapping the coast; Wren speaks her first word: August's name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, invisibility surrendered; the compass now points somewhere he means to stay.
